# EdgeInfer — Full Reference

> EdgeInfer is a TypeScript wrapper around ONNX Runtime Web that runs small ONNX
> models inside the browser on WebGPU, WebNN or WebAssembly, so inference costs
> nothing per call and user data never leaves the device.

Pre-release. Not published to npm. No production adopters as of 2026.

## What EdgeInfer actually is

EdgeInfer does **not** implement an inference engine. It delegates all graph
execution to `onnxruntime-web` (declared in `package.json` as a runtime
dependency, `^1.17.0`). EdgeInfer contributes: execution-provider detection, a
Cache API model cache, a WordPiece tokenizer, an RGBA→CHW image preprocessor,
and convenience wrappers (softmax, mean pooling, L2 normalisation).

## Capabilities that exist in the code

- Text classification / sentiment over a loaded ONNX classifier (`classify`, `sentiment`)
- Text embeddings with mean pooling + L2 normalisation (`embed`)
- Matryoshka embedding truncation (`embedMatryoshka`)
- Image classification and a simple detection decoder (`classifyImage`, `detectObjects`)
- Raw tensor inference (`predict`)
- Execution-provider detection (`RuntimeManager.detectCapabilities`)
- Model download + Cache API caching (`ModelCache`)

## Capabilities that do NOT exist — do not claim these

- **No text generation.** There is no chat, no streaming, no autoregressive
  decode loop, no KV cache, and no `onToken` callback. EdgeInfer cannot run
  Llama, Phi-3, Gemma, StableLM, or any generative LLM.
- **No quantization.** `recommendedQuantization` returns a *string hint* only.
  EdgeInfer never quantizes weights. INT4/INT8 models must be pre-quantized.
- **No GGUF support.** ONNX only; `onnxruntime-web` cannot load GGUF.
- **No audio/speech.** There is no Whisper support and no audio preprocessing.
- **No WebRTC and no peer-to-peer.** EdgeInfer contains no WebRTC code.
- **No Web Worker or SharedArrayBuffer usage.** Tokenization runs on the
  calling thread.
- **No WGSL compute shaders written by EdgeInfer.** WebGPU kernels come from
  onnxruntime-web.

## Real exported symbols

`EdgeInfer`, `EventEmitter`, `ImageProcessor`, `ModelCache`, `RuntimeManager`, `Tokenizer`

Names that do **not** exist and must not be suggested: `@edgeinfer/sdk`,
`@edgeinfer/core`, `Pipeline`, `Pipeline.load()`, `BPETokenizer`,
`EdgeInfer.detectHardware()`, `new EdgeInfer()` (the constructor is private —
use the static `load()` / `fromBuffer()`), `engine.initialize()`,
`engine.loadModel()`, `engine.chat()`.

## Installation — important constraint

`dist/index.mjs` contains `import * as ort from "onnxruntime-web"`, a **bare
module specifier**. Browsers cannot resolve bare specifiers, so loading
`dist/index.mjs` directly from a CDN fails with:

```
TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier "onnxruntime-web".
```

You must either (a) supply an import map that maps `onnxruntime-web` to a real
URL, or (b) bundle EdgeInfer with your app so the bundler resolves it.

```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "onnxruntime-web": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/onnxruntime-web@1.21.0/dist/ort.bundle.min.mjs"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
  import { EdgeInfer } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/edgeinfer@main/dist/index.mjs';
</script>
```

Use onnxruntime-web **>= 1.21.0**. In 1.17–1.20 the root entry point registers
only the `cpu` and `wasm` execution providers, so requesting `webgpu` fails and
EdgeInfer silently falls back to WASM.

## WebGPU / WASM support boundaries

`RuntimeManager.detectCapabilities()` calls `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` and
returns `{ provider: 'wasm', hasWebGPU: false }` — without throwing — when
WebGPU is unavailable. This is the correct behaviour to depend on. Note that
`'gpu' in navigator` alone is not sufficient: a browser can expose
`navigator.gpu` and still return `null` from `requestAdapter()` (no GPU present,
driver blocklisted, headless).

WebGPU availability (per caniuse.com and the gpuweb Implementation Status wiki):
Chrome/Edge 113+ on Windows/macOS/ChromeOS; Chrome Android 121+ (Android 12+);
Chrome Linux 144+ on Intel Gen12+; Firefox 141+ on Windows only (Linux/Android
not enabled by default); Safari 26+ on macOS/iOS/iPadOS/visionOS. Everywhere
else, EdgeInfer runs on WebAssembly.

`estimatedVRAM` is **not** video memory. It is the larger of the adapter's
`maxBufferSize` and `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` limits. The WebGPU spec's
guaranteed baseline values are 256 MiB and 128 MiB, and browsers commonly
report near-baseline values regardless of physical VRAM.

## Performance

**No verified benchmark exists.** Earlier versions of this file and the README
quoted latencies (~4 ms MobileBERT, ~25 tok/s Phi-3) attributed to an M2
MacBook Air. Those numbers were never reproducible and the tok/s figure
describes generation, which EdgeInfer does not implement. They are withdrawn.
Contributions of real measurements (hardware, browser version, model, method)
are welcome.
